about: Regular expressions in src/*.mjs and mcctl.mjs that the Rust regex crate cannot run as written: it has no lookaround and no backreferences. Each phase rewrites the ones in its modules, with a test that feeds both sides the same inputs. test/contracts-files.test.mjs scans the source and fails when this set changes (a new line, a moved one, or a pattern that no longer reads as listed), and when a new RegExp site appears that is not listed under constructed.

unsupported.what: INLINE_KEY: a key inside an inline YAML or JSON map, quoted with the same quote on both sides
PANEL_TOKEN: a panel sign-in token, redacted from a diagnostics bundle
account names and uuids redacted from a diagnostics bundle, as whole words
the Windows user name in a path, before a log goes to mclo.gs
IP_RE: player addresses in console lines, hidden from the assistant
PROJECT_ID: a Modrinth or Hangar project id that is not only dots
a server.properties value with \u not followed by four hex digits

runtime.policy: These take a pattern at run time in JavaScript's dialect. In Rust they run on the regex crate; a pattern that uses syntax it lacks (lookaround, backreferences, other JavaScript-only forms) is refused with a clear message, a declared difference. The Mojang patterns are checked against every manifest in the captured fixtures.

sites.what: the MCP get_logs tool's grep, case-insensitive
a bot scenario's /pattern/flags (expectMessage, waitWindow, present, absent); checked here, matched by src/bot-host.cjs, which stays JavaScript (bot-host.cjs:48)
a Mojang library or argument rule's os.version, matched against the OS version; a pattern that does not compile makes the rule not match

constructed.about: Every other new RegExp in the source builds its pattern from constants or escaped text, so the port writes an equivalent pattern by hand.
